parsed.summary: The file proves two things. First, there is a finite connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H on Fin q, with every colour class of every proper 2-colouring having a vertex of degree ≥ 2, and constants c, ε > 0 such that ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all sufficiently large n. Second, the Erdős degeneracy conjecture is false, stated as: not every bipartite r-degenerate graph (r > 0) satisfies ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}). Both match Theorem 1.2 and its stated consequence. The only deviation is an extra degree condition in the existential, which makes Lean slightly stronger and is harmless.

glossary.plain: N_G(v) ∩ s, the neighbours of v inside the finite set s
glossary.standard_concept: neighbourhood restricted to a vertex subset

glossary.plain: Every nonempty finite vertex set s contains a vertex v with |N(v) ∩ s| ≤ r, i.e. every nonempty induced subgraph has a vertex of degree ≤ r.
glossary.note: The paper says 'every nonempty subgraph'. Restricting to induced subgraphs is equivalent, since deleting edges only lowers degrees.

glossary.plain: For all r > 0 and every bipartite r-degenerate graph H on Fin q: ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}) as n → ∞.
glossary.note: Here r > 0, so 1/r carries no junk value. Mathlib's extremalNumber is the standard ex(n,H).

lean_claims.plain: There exist q and a graph H on Fin q such that: H is connected, bipartite and 2-degenerate; for every proper 2-colouring and each colour class, the maximum degree in that class is ≥ 2; and there are reals c > 0, ε > 0 with c·n^{3/2+ε} ≤ ex(n,H) for all sufficiently large n.
There exist r > 0 and a bipartite r-degenerate finite graph H such that ex(n,H) is not O(n^{2−1/r}).

paper_claims.plain: There exist a fixed connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H and constants c, ε > 0 with ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all sufficiently large n.
Erdős's conjecture that every bipartite r-degenerate H has ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}) is false, already for r = 2.
Failure of compactness (covered elsewhere, sibling file).

coverage.why: Lean adds the extra conclusion that each colour class has a vertex of degree ≥ 2; otherwise identical.
This is the direct negation of the conjecture as stated.

flags.explanation: There is an extra conjunct: in every 2-colouring, each colour class has max degree ≥ 2. The paper does not state this, but it follows for any counterexample. A connected bipartite H with superlinear ex must contain a cycle, and a cycle has degree-2 vertices on both sides. This strengthens the existential and so is harmless. Note it does NOT exclude the known Füredi/AKS case (one class has max degree ≤ r = 2).

lint_verdicts.why: The card is of a Finset, so there is no infinite-type junk value.
The hypothesis 0 < r ensures 1/(r:ℝ) is a genuine reciprocal.
